title: Where's Bernard
subject: a man whose pet tortoise Bernard escapes into the back garden and stays missing for three weeks while the whole family searches, until he finds him asleep inside his own wellington boot by the back door
caption: Appalachian old-time string band, porch-session revival style. Old-time fiddle sawing a driving reel with double stops, clawhammer banjo in open tuning, flatpicked acoustic guitar boom-chuck rhythm, upright bass on root and fifth, foot stomps on the beat. One-room live recording with mic bleed, raw and unpolished. Male baritone, plain folk delivery, rough group gang vocals on the chorus. 118 BPM, D major. Rollicking, comic and fond. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no autotune, no pop production, no bluegrass speed-picking showcase.
lyrics:
[Intro - fiddle and banjo]

[Verse 1]
Bernard took a walk one Tuesday
Slow as Sunday, out the gate
Ninety years he's got to live
So he's in no hurry, mate

[Chorus]
Where's Bernard, where'd he go
Not in the hedge, not in the peas
Lettuce on a saucer by the door
Where's Bernard, where's he gone

[Verse 2]
The kids put posters on the fence
My wife looked in the shed
We turned the compost twenty times
I looked under the bed

[Chorus]
Where's Bernard, where'd he go
Not by the bins, not in the rhubarb
Three weeks now and the lettuce is limp
Where's Bernard, where's he gone

[Bridge - fiddle break]
Then I went to pull my boots on
And my left boot wouldn't go

[Chorus]
There's Bernard, there he is
Snoring in my wellie
Three weeks by the back door
There's Bernard, home all along

[Outro - stomps and fiddle]
Slow as Sunday, Bernard
